sections.title: Objective Questions

sections.instructions: Answer each question in brief, showing your working.

questions.prompt: Solve the following pair of linear equations by the substitution method: x + y = 10 and x - y = 4.

value_points: From x - y = 4, take x = y + 4 (or an equivalent first step)
Substituting in x + y = 10 gives (y + 4) + y = 10, so y = 3
Then x = 7; solution x = 7, y = 3

questions.prompt: Find a quadratic polynomial whose zeroes are 3 and -2.

value_points: Sum of zeroes = 3 + (-2) = 1; product of zeroes = 3 x (-2) = -6
The polynomial is x^2 - (sum of zeroes)x + (product of zeroes)
So the polynomial is x^2 - x - 6 (any non-zero multiple is acceptable)

questions.prompt: Find the sum of the first 20 terms of the AP 5, 8, 11, ...

value_points: Here a = 5, d = 3, n = 20

questions.prompt: Prove that 1 + tan^2 A = sec^2 A.

value_points: Write tan A = sin A / cos A, so 1 + tan^2 A = 1 + sin^2 A / cos^2 A
Combining: = (cos^2 A + sin^2 A) / cos^2 A
Using sin^2 A + cos^2 A = 1 gives 1 / cos^2 A = sec^2 A

questions.prompt: Find the area of a sector of a circle of radius 14 cm, where the angle of the sector is 90 degrees.

value_points: Area of a sector = (angle / 360) x pi x r^2

questions.prompt: Find the median of the following data: 12, 15, 11, 20, 18, 14, 16.

value_points: Arranging in ascending order: 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, 18, 20
There are 7 observations, so the median is the 4th observation
Median = 15

sections.title: Short Answers I

sections.instructions: Answer each question, showing all the steps of your working.

questions.prompt: Divide the polynomial 3x^2 + 5x - 4 by x + 2 and write down the quotient and the remainder.

value_points: First step: 3x^2 divided by x gives 3x; multiply back and subtract to get -x - 4
Second step: -x divided by x gives -1; multiply back and subtract
Quotient = 3x - 1
Remainder = -2

questions.prompt: Find the coordinates of the point which divides the line segment joining (2, -3) and (8, 3) internally in the ratio 2 : 1.

value_points: Using the section formula with m : n = 2 : 1
The required point is (6, 1)

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, a line DE is drawn parallel to BC, with D on AB and E on AC. If AD = 3 cm, DB = 6 cm and AE = 4 cm, find EC.

value_points: By the Basic Proportionality Theorem, AD / DB = AE / EC
Substituting: 3 / 6 = 4 / EC
So EC = (6 x 4) / 3
EC = 8 cm

questions.prompt: From a point on the ground, 30 m away from the foot of a tower, the angle of elevation of the top of the tower is 60 degrees. Find the height of the tower.

value_points: Let h be the height of the tower; the tower, the ground, and the line of sight form a right-angled triangle
tan 60 degrees = h / 30
So h = 30 x tan 60 degrees = 30 x square root of 3
Height of the tower = 30 x 1.732 = 51.96 m (approximately)

questions.prompt: A solid cylinder has radius 7 cm and height 20 cm. Find its total surface area.

value_points: Total surface area of a cylinder = 2 x pi x r x (r + h)

questions.prompt: Two dice are thrown at the same time. Find the probability that the sum of the numbers appearing on them is 8.

value_points: Total number of possible outcomes = 6 x 6 = 36
Number of favourable outcomes = 5
Required probability = 5 / 36

sections.title: Short Answers II

sections.instructions: Answer each question in detail. Internal choice is given in Q34.

questions.prompt: The area of a rectangular plot is 528 m^2. The length of the plot is one more than twice its breadth. Find the length and the breadth of the plot.

value_points: Let the breadth be b m; then the length is (2b + 1) m
Area: b(2b + 1) = 528, giving 2b^2 + b - 528 = 0
Discriminant = 1 + 4 x 2 x 528 = 4225 = 65^2, so b = (-1 + 65) / 4 = 16 (rejecting the negative root)
Breadth = 16 m
Length = 2 x 16 + 1 = 33 m (check: 16 x 33 = 528)

choice.alternative_prompt: Prove that the angle between the two tangents drawn from an external point to a circle is supplementary to the angle subtended by the line segment joining the points of contact at the centre of the circle.

questions.prompt: Prove that the lengths of the tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal.

alternative_value_points: Let the external point be P, the centre O, and the points of contact A and B
In quadrilateral OAPB, the angles at A and B are each 90 degrees, since a radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact
So the sum of the remaining angles: APB + AOB = 360 - 90 - 90
Therefore angle APB + angle AOB = 180 degrees
Hence the angle between the tangents is supplementary to the angle at the centre
value_points: Figure and given: external point P, centre O, points of contact A and B; OA and OB joined, OP joined
In triangles OAP and OBP: OA = OB (radii of the same circle)
Angle OAP = angle OBP = 90 degrees (radius perpendicular to tangent)
OP is common, so the triangles are congruent by RHS
Therefore PA = PB by CPCT: the two tangents are equal in length

questions.prompt: The following distribution shows the daily pocket allowance (in rupees) of the children of a locality. Find the mean daily pocket allowance. Daily allowance: 11-13 (7 children), 13-15 (6), 15-17 (9), 17-19 (13), 19-21 (20), 21-23 (5), 23-25 (4).

value_points: Class marks of the classes are 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24
Products of frequency and class mark: 84, 84, 144, 234, 400, 110, 96
Sum of frequencies = 64; sum of the products = 1152
Mean daily pocket allowance = 18 rupees
